# Ether plugin reference

> Build EPP/1 plugins with the exact shipped manifest, SDK and host-service contracts.

Generated by go generate ./internal/plugins/devreference. Do not edit generated files.
Developer documentation and API vocabulary are in English. Capabilities describe behavior; permissions grant access. Hosted QuickJS is not Node.

Full contract: [llms-full.txt](/ether/plugins/reference/llms-full.txt)

## Authoring guide

# Build an Ether plugin

## The mental model (read this first)

A plugin is a manifest plus a request handler. **Kind** decides where the owner
finds it; **capabilities** advertise behavior; **contributes** describes that
behavior; **permissions** request access. A capability never grants permission.
Hosted TypeScript/JavaScript runs in QuickJS inside wazero, not Node: no process,
filesystem, npm resolution, or direct network. Export `handle(req)` returning
`{status, headers?, body}`. Use the synchronous permission-checked `ether` global.
Bundle SDK imports before packaging. Go/Python can run as HTTP/tunnel sidecars;
remote plugins have their own OS permissions and cannot use hosted folders or
SecretGet. Read current settings per request; persist state in KV, not globals.
Start with one useful result. Do work only on a viewer/owner request or an
explicitly configured job; page results and bound work so playback comes first.

The schema and generated reference are authoritative. Do not invent APIs from
method names. Open `/ether/plugins/reference/getting-started` in your server,
then search for the exact symbol. [Reference maintenance](../docs/plugin-developer-reference.md).

## Files

```text
my-plugin/
  manifest.json               # identity, runtime, permissions, contributions
  src/index.ts                # hosted handler (or plugin.py for a sidecar)
  dist/plugin.js              # compiled hosted artifact, generated by pack/load
  settings.schema.json        # referenced by ether.settings.$ref
  i18n/en.json                # English fallback for every $t:key
  assets/icon.svg             # optional icon
  tests/fixtures.json         # recorded request/expected-response cases
  README.md                   # setup and permission explanation
```

Paths in the manifest are package-relative and must stay inside the package.
Never ship credentials, node_modules, private media, or absolute local paths.

## First run: exact commands

From an Ether checkout, build the CLI once (pure Go):

```sh
CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o ./ether ./cmd/ether
./ether plugin new --kind integration --lang ts ./my-plugin
./ether plugin check ./my-plugin
./ether plugin test ./my-plugin
./ether plugin pack -o ./my-plugin.etherpkg ./my-plugin
```

With a **local development server you control** already running, set ETHER_TOKEN
to its admin token in your shell and run:

```sh
./ether plugin dev ./my-plugin --server http://localhost:32400
# Save src/index.ts: compile, install, and read logs. Ctrl-C stops watching.
# One install without a watcher:
./ether plugin dev ./my-plugin --server http://localhost:32400 --once
```

Alternatively open Plugins → Add plugin and upload `my-plugin.etherpkg`. Review
requested permissions and enable it. Do not use a production server for iteration.
`check --json` is the structured report for agents. `test` also runs recorded
fixtures; ETHER_BIN enables its headless integration check, ETHER_PLUGIN_URL tests
an already running remote sidecar. `pack` compiles TypeScript and checks the
package. No separate npm install is needed for generated hosted templates.

## Manifest decisions

| Field | What to set |
|---|---|
| id, version, name | Stable lower-case reverse DNS ID, SemVer, readable name (≤60 characters) |
| description | Sentence case, ≤300 characters |
| types, resources, catalogs, idPrefixes | Stremio types, routes, catalog IDs and identifier prefixes actually served |
| ether.protocol | `1` |
| ether.kind | `source`, `integration`, `notification_channel`, `livetv_source`, `extension`, or `content` |
| ether.capabilities | Only implemented capabilities; the validator checks allowed kinds |
| ether.summary | ≤80 characters, or `$t:summary` with English fallback |
| ether.runtime | Hosted: `{kind:"hosted",entry:"src/index.ts"}` (or WASM `module`); remote: `{kind:"remote"}` |
| ether.permissions | Network hostnames (not URLs), catalog `read`, collections `write`, folders `read`, named secrets, viewers, sources `search`/`acquire`; omit access you do not need |
| ether.settings | Inline `{fields:[...]}` or `{"$ref":"settings.schema.json"}` |
| ether.strings | Locale → package file or inline object; `en` required for `$t:` labels |
| ether.contributes | Capability descriptors, pages, slots, commands, setup steps, mediaKinds; see generated types |
| ether.schedule | `[{every:"1h",call:"/ether/refresh"}]`; intervals ≥15 minutes, bounded idempotent work |
| ether.cluster | `leader` (default), or `every_node` only when each node must run it |
| ether.health | Optional interval ≥15 seconds |
| ether.author, license, repo, icon | Attribution, SPDX license, repository URL, SVG path |
| ether.sidecar | Remote launch instructions: docker, download, command, docs |
| ether.stremio | `true` for a native plugin that retains Stremio add-on routes |

Copy rules apply to contribution labels too: sentence case, no exclamation marks,
no em/en dashes, no “simply”, “just”, or “easily”. Setting secrets are sealed by
Ether; read with SecretGet only where needed, never echo them into views/logs.

## Capability → routes → host services

| Capability | Plugin surface | Host services commonly needed |
|---|---|---|
| list_source | contributes.listSources + `/catalog/{type}/{id}.json` | HTTPFetch, CatalogSearch/Get, KV |
| catalog_provider | mediaKinds; paged browse/changes or push | KindUpsert/Delete/Items, KV |
| kind_resolver / matcher | kind resolve/match handlers | ResolveSources, CachePut/Open; sources permission |
| stream_source / debrid_provider | Stremio stream; lazy open / debrid routes | HTTPFetch, SecretGet |
| metadata | `/meta/{type}/{id}.json`, contributes.metadata | HTTPFetch, CatalogGet |
| notify / events | notify send/test; event subscription + acknowledgement | HTTPFetch, SecretGet, KV for deduplication |
| ui / tools | ViewSpec page/action or declared tool | Settings, KV; grant only data the action needs |
| livetv_channels | channels, guide, stream | HTTPFetch, KV |
| subtitles / markers | subtitle or marker routes and descriptors | HTTPFetch; download only after viewer picks |
| ranking_step / rule_condition | `rank_key` / `cond_match` | Log/abort only: deterministic, no I/O or clock |
| plugin_directory | declared add-on directories | HTTPFetch |
| frontend_adapter | authenticated protocol routes | StreamURL for own items; Ether serves bytes |
| onair_content / livetv_pack | declared feeds/segments/TV packs | Only services the handler actually needs |

Settings, KV, Log and NotifyOwner do not require an extra behavior capability.
FoldersList/Stat/Hash need `folders:read` plus an owner-selected root; they return
metadata/digests, not bytes. Viewer access requires that viewer's grant.
Host calls enforce permissions again on every request; revocation is immediate.

## Ten recipes

Commands below run from the repo root. Existing examples are living recipes;
keep their relative SDK imports at the same directory depth, bundle before
shipping, change the reverse-DNS ID before installing a copy alongside its source.
Read the named handler and its manifest together. Run `./ether plugin check DIR`
and `./ether plugin pack DIR` after editing each recipe.

### 1. Catalogue source

```sh
./ether plugin new --kind integration --lang ts ./my-catalogue
```

Replace the generated `/catalog/` branch's empty `metas` with a small bounded
list of `{id:"tt0133093",type:"movie",name:"The Matrix"}`. Keep the listSources
catalog ID (`featured`) aligned with `/catalog/movie/featured.json`. Full typed
catalogue/meta handlers: `sdk/examples/hello/typescript/plugin.ts`.

### 2. A content kind library

```sh
cp -R sdk/examples/kind-library sdk/examples/my-library
./ether plugin check sdk/examples/my-library
```

Edit mediaKinds levels, fields and presentation, then the browse/changes/resolve
handlers in `src/plugin.ts`. Keep cursor pages bounded and item IDs stable. Read
[Content kinds](../docs/plugin-kinds.md) before changing resolve or container semantics.

### 3. Resolver / playable source

```sh
./ether plugin new --kind source --lang ts ./my-source
```

Fill `/stream/{type}/{id}.json` with `{streams:[{url:"https://YOUR_HOST/video.mp4"}]}`
using an owner-configured source, not hard-coded credentials. Declare YOUR_HOST
in network permissions if the plugin fetches it. Return lazy stream descriptors
for work that should happen only on a viewer pick. See `sdk/examples/easydebrid`.

### 4. Notification channel

```sh
./ether plugin new --kind notification_channel --lang ts ./my-notifier
```

Implement the notify send and send-test handlers; the generated event handler
shows acknowledgement IDs. Declare webhook hosts and named secrets. Deduplicate
events by ID before sending; a retried outbox delivery must not send twice.

### 5. Page and action

```sh
cp -R sdk/examples/movie-night sdk/examples/my-page
./ether plugin check sdk/examples/my-page
```

Edit the ViewSpec and action in `src/plugin.ts`. Keep labels in i18n files and
use stable action IDs. This example saves a shortlist in KV on an explicit pick;
opening a page should read saved data, not repeatedly scan the catalogue.

### 6. Scheduled job

```sh
./ether plugin new --kind integration --lang ts ./my-job
```

Add `ether.schedule: [{"every":"1h","call":"/ether/refresh"}]` to the manifest
and handle that path. Store a cursor/etag in KV and process a bounded batch per
run. Do not create timers in plugin code. Cache external results; keep the job
unconfigured until the owner needs it. Settings changes must be read each run.

### 7. Settings and setup steps

```sh
cp -R sdk/examples/kind-library sdk/examples/my-setup
```

Edit `settings.schema.json`, `contributes.setup.steps`, and `/ether/v1/setup/…/test`
together. Required setup gates library sync until passed or owner-skipped. Use
field-keyed validation errors, never secrets in test responses. The generated
integration template also demonstrates `$ref` settings with translated labels.

### 8. Folder reader

```sh
cp -R sdk/examples/local-folders sdk/examples/my-folders
```

Follow `plugin.ts`: ask for a folder setting and `folders:read`, walk only that
root, store an index in KV, and rescan on the owner's action. Owner-selected root
handles are not arbitrary paths. Hash large files with the pollable hash API;
never block a playback request to hash or walk a tree.

### 9. Metadata and artwork

```sh
cp -R sdk/examples/hello sdk/examples/my-metadata
```

Use `typescript/plugin.ts`'s meta route (or `go/plugin.go`) as the typed starting
point. Return supported poster/background URLs in metadata. For a canonical
metadata provider add the `metadata` capability and its descriptor from the
reference. **`artwork` is reserved**: do not claim it as a capability. Hosted
requests for images require their hostname in network permissions.

### 10. Stremio-style add-on bridge

```sh
cp -R sdk/examples/hello sdk/examples/my-addon
```

The typed hello implementations serve catalog/meta/subtitles routes. A plain
Stremio manifest without `ether` is already supported: install its manifest URL
through Add plugin. If you add native Ether settings/UI, retain the Stremio
fields and set `ether.stremio:true`; Ether derives roles from those resources.
Do not rewrite IDs or response envelopes. Go sidecar from the copied example:

```sh
CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./sdk/examples/my-addon/go/...
# Original runnable sidecar:
CGO_ENABLED=0 go run ./sdk/examples/hello/go/cmd
```

## Fast fixes

| Symptom | Why / exact next step |
|---|---|
| Unknown capability / wrong kind | Check the capability table and change ether.kind or remove the unsupported capability; artwork/ratings are reserved |
| Cannot import module in hosted runtime | Bundle local SDK imports into the entry artifact; no npm resolution in QuickJS |
| `ether` / process / fs unavailable | Use hosted host services, or choose a remote sidecar for OS APIs |
| Permission denied | Declare the exact permission/hostname, reinstall, then have the owner grant it; never retry around revocation |
| Missing settings/strings file | Include the $ref/i18n path inside the package; run check again |
| Empty content library | Complete required setup, enable the plugin, check sync cursors and its mediaKind descriptors |
| Conformance route failed | Read rule + field + route; implement its exact response shape from Reference → Capabilities, then rerun check |
| Dev 401/403 | Set ETHER_TOKEN to the local server's admin token and review its requested grants |
| Dev connection refused | Start your local server and pass its actual --server URL/port |
| Dev install conflicts | Check existing plugin ID/version; do not change identity on every save |
| Labels rejected | Sentence case, length limits, no banned words/punctuation; translate every referenced key |

Before reporting success: review the diff, compile the chosen language, run
conformance, package, and check the visible result on your own development server.
Never claim offline conformance proves playback on a real client. New host
services belong in the generated reference source list and this service map;
regenerate the reference instead of duplicating contracts in prose.
